question: Can a reverse policy satisfy the independent acceptance gate: 10 s upright on 5 perturbed seeds AND mean reverse speed at least half the -0.074 m/s command?
gate: duration >= 10 s, 5/5 seeds, |mean forward speed| >= 0.037 m/s
method: validate_backward_sustained.py, native MuJoCo, unchanged flat-terrain XML, motor slew limit on, 3 s standing warm-up, independent +/-0.02 qvel perturbations per seed, command -0.074 m/s

runs.verdict: Fails: fast reverse (-0.112) but falls at ~1.55 s. Penalising the COM-behind-support precursor alone does not fix it.

runs.reward_terms: rear support-shortfall + single support + swing rear foot reward
runs.verdict: FIRST REVERSE POLICY TO PASS THE STABILITY HALF: 5/5 upright for the full window. Speed -0.028 is below the 0.037 requirement, so the gate as a whole is not met yet.

runs.reward_terms: v30 contact group + heading error + yaw error + lin-vel XY error
runs.verdict: Regression: adding the heading/yaw/lin-vel group on top of v30 drops completion from 5/5 to 1/5.

conclusion: Contact-aware stepping (v30) is the first mechanism to buy sustained reverse stability, confirming the 2026-09-26 prediction that the failure is rear foot placement and pitch recovery rather than reward magnitude. The remaining gap is speed: v30 trades speed for stability. The heading constraints in v31 are counterproductive on top of v30 and should not be used when pursuing speed.
next: v32 restores v30's contact group, drops the v31 heading group, and raises only the two speed-pressure terms (normalized_progress / progress_shortfall) to 2x and 4x.
